artists.biography: Mudhoney is an American alternative rock band. Formed in Seattle, Washington, in 1988 following the demise of Green River, Mudhoney's members are vocalist and rhythm guitarist Mark Arm, lead guitarist Steve Turner, bassist Guy Maddison, and drummer Dan Peters. Original bassist Matt Lukin left the band in 1999 but briefly returned in December 2000 to complete touring obligations. Mudhoney's early releases on Sub Pop, particularly debut single "Touch Me I'm Sick" and the Superfuzz Bigmuff EP, were massively influential on the Seattle music scene, helping more than almost any other releases of the era to inspire the dirty, high-distortion sound that would become grunge. Mudhoney was also notable for its mixing of heavy blues rock and punk rock. Although the band has found little commercial success during its long career, which has yielded 10 studio albums, it nonetheless inspired many grunge and alternative rock musicians.

perplexity.description:
Digital Garbage is the tenth studio album by American rock band Mudhoney, released on September 28, 2018, through Sub Pop Records. The album marks the band's return after a five-year gap since their previous full-length, Vanishing Point (2013), and stands as their seventh release on Sub Pop. Musically, Digital Garbage continues Mudhoney’s signature blend of gritty garage rock, punk energy, and melodic alt-rock, characterized by Mark Arm’s raw vocals and the band’s tight, dynamic instrumentation. The album’s sound is both a nod to their grunge roots and a reflection of their evolution, with tracks that balance aggression and melody, often underscored by social commentary and a sense of urgency.

In the context of Mudhoney’s discography, Digital Garbage reaffirms their status as enduring figures in the Pacific Northwest rock scene. The album was well-received by critics, who praised its consistency, energy, and the band’s ability to maintain their distinctive style while addressing contemporary themes. Reviews highlighted the album’s sharp songwriting and the chemistry between band members, noting that it stands among their strongest later-career releases. Commercially, it performed solidly for an indie rock album, further cementing Mudhoney’s legacy as influential veterans of the genre.
